🇶🇦Qatar set to become world's largest buyer of US LNG amid Iran war disruptions
Qatar, one of the world's leading natural gas exporters, is set to become the largest buyer of US liquefied natural gas (LNG), securing supplies outside the Persian Gulf as the war involving Iran disrupts its own exports, the Financial Times reports.
By 2033, QatarE nergy is expected to control 23.7M tons of US LNG annually. Two agreements signed in October added 7M tons a year to its portfolio, alongside production from the company's 70% stake in the Golden Pass LNG project in Texas.
The shift follows disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz during the US-Israeli war with Iran, which have reportedly reduced Qatar's LNG exports to less than a third of normal levels.
The US gas will be resold to international customers rather than consumed in Qatar. Deliveries under the new contracts begin in 2030 and 2031, providing a longer-term alternative to supplies vulnerable to disruptions in the Persian Gulf.

🇺🇸✈️ Rare US spy plane reportedly crosses Atlantic amid Iran strike speculation
A US Air Force Boeing RC-135U reconnaissance aircraft (64-14849) has reportedly departed Offutt Air Force Base and crossed the Atlantic, according to OSINT accounts. Its destination remains unknown.
One of only two aircraft of its kind in the US fleet, the RC-135U specializes in detecting and analyzing radar emissions, including those from air defense systems, to help develop electronic countermeasures.
The reported flight comes amid reports of possible renewed US strikes on Iran following the November 3 midterm elections. ABC News previously reported preparations for possible post-election attacks, while AP reported warnings to regional allies about potential escalation and Iranian retaliation.
Trump, however, assured the Financial Times on November 4 that no immediate strikes on Iran were planned.
